hero-split.title: Stairs that outlive the house
hero-split.lede: Two joiners, one workshop in Bristol, and a waiting list we keep honest. Every flight is drawn, cut and fitted by the people who answer the phone.
hero-split.image_alt: A joiner easing the nosing on an oak stair tread

hero-type.title: We build the part you touch
hero-type.lede: Handrails, stairs and doors, cut from stock we chose ourselves and fitted by the two people who drew them.

hero-bleed.title: Fifty winters of stock, seasoned in the same shed
hero-bleed.lede: We buy the tree, not the board. What leaves the workshop has been in Bristol longer than most of the houses it goes into.
hero-bleed.image_alt: Stacked and stickered oak boards seasoning in an open timber shed

proof-row.title: The numbers our accountant will confirm
proof-row.marquee_label: Architects and builders we work with

feature-zigzag.title: Drawn in the house, cut in the shed
feature-zigzag.feature_1_body: Someone comes out with a laser and a notebook and measures the opening you actually have, not the one on the plan. The quote that follows is the price you pay, and if the floor turns out to be two degrees off we tell you that day.
feature-zigzag.feature_1_image_alt: A joiner taking measurements in a stripped hallway
feature-zigzag.feature_2_title: Fitted by the pair who made it
feature-zigzag.feature_2_body: No subcontracted fitting team, no handover. The two people who cut your strings carry them up the path, which is why the tolerances hold and why nobody has to blame anyone else when a wall is not plumb.
feature-zigzag.feature_2_image_alt: Two joiners easing a finished stair flight into a hallway

process-rail.kicker: From first call to first step
process-rail.title: Four visits, and you meet the same two people at each
process-rail.lede: Most staircase jobs take fourteen weeks. Here is where the time goes, so you can plan the rest of the build around it.
process-rail.step_1_body: Two hours in the house with a laser and a notebook. We measure the opening, the headroom and the floor you have, then leave you a fixed price.
process-rail.step_2_body: A full-size rod drawn on the shop floor and a set of sections for you. Nothing is cut until you have signed the drawing you can actually read.
process-rail.step_3_body: Six to eight weeks in the shed. Strings, treads and handrail are cut from one parcel of timber so the grain and the colour run through the whole flight.
process-rail.step_4_body: Three days on site with the pair who built it. We take the old flight out, put the new one in, and leave with the offcuts and the dust.

offer-table.title: Two ways to buy a staircase
offer-table.lede: Both prices include the survey, the drawing and the fitting. Neither includes plaster repair, because we cannot see your walls from here.
offer-table.table_caption: Prices held until 31 March 2026. Compare across a row.
offer-table.plan_2_note: Oak or ash, cut strings, oiled
offer-table.footnote: Prices exclude VAT and any plaster or electrical work the removal exposes. We will tell you what we can see at the survey and what we cannot see until the old flight is out.

testimonial-pair.title: What the people who paid for it said
testimonial-pair.quote_1: They found the floor was out by eleven millimetres and told us at the survey, not on the invoice. The stairs went in on the Tuesday they said they would, in the week they said they would.
testimonial-pair.quote_2: We had three quotes. Theirs was not the cheapest and it was the only one with a drawing attached. Two years on, not one tread has moved or made a sound.

faq-list.title: The five things everybody asks
faq-list.lede: If the answer you need is not here, ring the workshop. The phone is on the bench and one of us picks it up.
faq-list.q1: How long will we be without a staircase?
faq-list.a1: Three days, and you keep a temporary flight the whole time. We take the old one out on the Monday morning, the new one goes in that afternoon, and Tuesday and Wednesday are handrail, balusters and making good.
faq-list.q2: Do you need the house empty?
faq-list.a2: No. We need the hallway clear and a parking space within about thirty metres. People carry on living upstairs through the whole fit, and we sheet everything on the route in.
faq-list.q3: Can you match a staircase we already have?
faq-list.a3: Usually. Bring us a photograph and, if you can, a section of the existing handrail. We cut our own moulding cutters, so a profile nobody stocks any more is not the problem it sounds like.
faq-list.a4: The quote is fixed on what we could measure at the survey. What we cannot see is the state of the wall behind the old strings, so plaster repair is quoted separately once the flight is out.
faq-list.a5: Ring us. The guarantee runs ten years on parts and labour, and a squeak in year four is still ours to fix. Nine callbacks in ten years is the record we would like to keep.

closing-block.title: Come and see the timber before you commit
closing-block.lede: The workshop is open on weekdays and most Saturday mornings. Bring the dimensions you have, or none at all.
closing-block.aside: We answer the phone between seven and five, weekdays. A survey is free and takes about two hours, and you get the fixed price within three working days.
